method: paired mean difference with two-sided 95% Student-t confidence interval
evidence_scope: Exploratory screen over the standard-window length under processed-block semantics. Screening on 100 paired seeds can rank the arms, but a selected length needs confirmation on disjoint seeds before adoption, and this run cannot establish equivalence or show that an unobserved practically important effect is absent.
difference_direction: candidate arm minus reference arm, per contrast

notes: All window arms take the standard controller's utilisation window over processed-block summaries only (non-certificate RBs, certificate-carrying RBs, certified EBs); the historical arm's window additionally lets zero-width EbAnnounced entries occupy positions, which shortens its effective depth at contended loads. The window arms differ from the historical arm only in the standard signal.

Announcement entries are not adoptable in the ledger rule: an announcement is a costless, unpunishable producer claim, so counting it would hand producers a free lever on the standard quote. The screen asks which fixed processed-block length best approximates the historical behaviour.

Launch day is the decision-facing load: the announcement-semantics smoke measured the 20-processed-block window losing about 1.5 percentage points of overall retained-value ratio there against the historical arm. Low and mid load are expected to be bit-identical across window arms (the standard coefficient rests on its floor).
Flat-fee contrasts give the adoption floor: a window length is only acceptable if the mechanism keeps its improvement over flat fee at the contended loads.
Independent streams align fresh-demand samples and Ranking Block opportunities within a seed; retry jitter remains mechanism-dependent.
Launch-day urgent-class slices are omitted because that profile changes the urgency-rate multiplier over time; priority-lane metrics remain usable.
